@graph.nrr:hypothesis: Use synthesis-energy calculations, machine-learning classifiers and de novo design over more than 10,000 organic structure-directing agents to find OSDAs that would crystallise the aluminosilicate forms of the STF and IFR zeolites in hydroxide media, then test the shortlist hydrothermally.
nrr:invalidators: crystallisation of aluminosilicate STF or IFR in hydroxide media with any of the shortlisted OSDAs once OSDA stability is controlled
a positive-control synthesis showing the protocol yields a known phase, which would turn the amorphous results into evidence against the predictions
a synthesis-energy model including OSDA degradation, solvation and counter-cations that predicts the amorphous outcomes
nrr:nextSteps: Include solvent effects, especially how water and counter-cations influence framework stability and OSDA-framework interaction, in the phase prediction.
Examine OSDA stability under hydrothermal conditions, since degradation during synthesis can prevent structure direction.
Link computational insight with experimental feedback to guide zeolite crystallisation.
nrr:openQuestions: Can aluminosilicate STF or IFR be crystallised in hydroxide media at all, given that CHA and AEI are predicted to be more stable for every OSDA screened?
Would the predicted phases (CHA, AEI) have formed if the OSDAs had survived the hydrothermal conditions?
@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: Experimental synthesis using a shortlist of OSDAs predicted to favor STF or IFR, in addition to AEI or CHA, did not yield the expected aluminosilicate products, and instead, amorphous materials were obtained in most cases. our experiments did not result in AEI or CHA being synthesized (neither STF nor IFR), and hence in this sense our predictions from calculations must be considered a failure.
nrr:provenanceNotes: The STF OSDA was obtained as a mixture of stereoisomers: obtained as a mixture of four diastereomers (eight configurations); the computed isomer is about one quarter of the cations present; attempts to isolate single isomers failed (SI Section S9, Table S19). Its elemental analysis is off: Anal. calcd C 54.96, H 9.23, N 5.34; found C 49.24, H 9.50, N 5.03 (SI Section S8).

Source inconsistency on the first IFR OSDA: SI Section S8 says 'the cyclohexyl-derived organic cation was synthesized as an alternative'; the compound made, named and characterised is the N-benzyl (phenyl) cation, as main-text Table 2 states.

Table 2 (image in the XML) reports QG001780m2 as 'amorphous (Table S22) and amorphous + MTW (Table S21)'; Table S21 also lists MOR and dense phases and Table S22 lists MOR and a dense phase, which Table 2 and the Discussion do not mention
The article has no author-contribution statement; every author is recorded with the role 'writing' only.

Table 1 of the article is machine-readable in the JATS XML; Table 2 is an image and was transcribed from the PMC figure file; the synthesis outcomes come from SI Tables S18, S20, S21 and S22, which are text in the PDF.

The computational screen's sensitivity and specificity figures (SI Tables S7 to S12) are recorded as findings about the classifiers. The ingest does not count them as a sensitivity statement for the hydrothermal findings, because they describe the classifier's recall on literature OSDAs, not the synthesis's ability to detect a crystalline phase.
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: A hydrothermal synthesis in hydroxide media whose powder X-ray diffraction pattern matches aluminosilicate STF or IFR, with an OSDA predicted by synthesis energy to favour that phase.
